text:
jonah: ping — customer (acme-inc) saw a flurry of 429s during a ~30s microburst even though they have burst cushion on their hosted plan. Headers they pasted:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 100
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-Burst-Credits: 0
X-Burst-Refill-At: 2025-03-10T15:42:12Z
```
jonah: pattern was: short-lived ramp to ~150 req/s for ~20s, then back to normal. region=us-east, model=gpt-open-7b, route=/v1/generate
mira: are they on payg or a reserved/dedicated pool?
jonah: payg, account id 64211. They said they saw 429s for ~12s mid-spike. No client-side retries initially.
devon: can you paste the exact client loop? curious if they sent many parallel connections vs serialized requests.
jonah: here is the repro snippet they used:
```bash
seq 1 150 | xargs -n1 -P150 -I{} curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"input":"hi"}'
```
kai: that parallel xargs pattern will blow through the bucket. Our smoothing/refill math is per-account and has a small refill quantum that can make short microbursts exhaust visible credits. Also fractional refill behavior differs by plan.
kai: internal note on config (approx):
```
burst_bucket_size: 200           # max stored credits
refill_rate_per_min: 6000       # tokens per minute (100/s)
refill_granularity_ms: 1000     # refills happen each 1s in quanta
smoothing_window_ms: 1000      # short window we smooth against
jitter_threshold: 0.2           # clients within 20% jitter are considered bursty
```
devon: two angles: short-term fixes for the customer + long-term platform tuning. Short-term: ask them to add tiny client-side smoothing (random sleep 5-10ms or limit concurrency) and enable exponential backoff with jitter. That eliminates microburst drain.
mira: what should we tell them about burst credits? customer asked why credits were 0 while they thought cushion would cover this.
kai: explain that credits are consumed by peak concurrency and refill only in quanta — a 20s surge at 150r/s will deplete a 200-credit bucket fast; fractional refill within that second isn't applied so you can hit 0 inside the second. Also mention per-route caps and safety headroom.
jonah: drafting reply: "Short microbursts can still produce transient 429s if concurrency exceeds the instantaneous available credits because refill happens in discrete quanta. Recommend limiting parallel requests to ~80-100/s or add client-side jitter; we can also preview a dedicated baseline for predictable throughput."
devon: add a repro note for eng: capture X-Burst-Credits and X-Burst-Refill headers during the spike, and a pprof of the token-bucket meter if we can reproduce on staging. I'll open a small infra ticket to add higher-resolution metrics for refill timing.
mira: for support reply include a short config sample for client smoothing:
```js
// simple JS limiter
const qps = 90;
await Promise.all(requests.map((req, i) => new Promise(r => setTimeout(async () => { await call(req); r(); }, (i / qps) * 1000 + Math.random()*30))));
```
mira: ok sending that + explanation + 20% promo credit for churn risk :white_check_mark:
jonah: customer accepted the smoothing change and will roll it this afternoon. They appreciated the explanation.
support-bot: Created ticket #SUP-2025-789 for infra to investigate refill granularity and telemetry.
devon: tagging @kai to follow up on filing a small perf/metrics spike so we can see per-ms refill events in staging.
kai: got it — will prioritize after standup.
